results.title: Creality presents multi-tool creation ecosystem and new hardware range at RAPID + TCT 2026 | VoxelMatters - The heart of additive manufacturing
excerpts:
voxelmatters.directory/company/creality/) took full advantage of its appearance at RAPID + TCT 2026 in Boston this week to present its broad hardware and software portfolio spanning 3D printing, 3D scanning, laser processing, filament recycling, and cloud-based management.

The company’s end-to-end workflow line-up, which connects each stage of the manufacturing process from physical object capture through to finished part production, was in full demo mode as it gave the North American market a hands-on opportunity to see its range – including recent launches – up close.

Among the hardware on display was the [SPARKX i7, which was officially launched at CES in Las Vegas at the start of the year](https://www.voxelmatters.com/creality-introduces-sparkx-i7-desktop-3d-printer-with-for-affordable-multicolor-printing/) .
The fused filament fabrication (FFF) printer features a quick-swap hotend, a redesigned color-changing mechanism, and a four-color filament system to serve up a desktop configuration that reduces material waste. The printer supports AI-assisted model generation, print monitoring, and mobile operation.

Creality also presented the [Filament Maker M1 and Shredder R1, launched on Indiegogo earlier this month](https://www.voxelmatters.com/creality-launches-filament-maker-m1-shredder-r1/) , and which it claims is the first integrated desktop system designed to recycle waste plastic and produce custom filament. The crowdfunding campaign for the product has to date [raised just under HK$45 million](https://www.indiegogo.com/en/projects/creality/creality-filament-maker-m1--shredder-r1?refcode=gwihVw-3Fky0Js9OUKPg7A) ( $5.7m).

[](https://www.voxelmatters.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Creality-Rapid-TCT-03.jpg) [](https://www.voxelmatters.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Creality-Rapid-TCT-02.

...

It also scans black and reflective metal surfaces without requiring powder coating, and covers objects ranging from 5 mm³ to 4,000 mm³.

Creality also highlighted the addition of MagicRelief to its cloud platform. The AI tool converts photographs into printable relief artwork without requiring prior modeling experience or external software.

results.title: Creality Marks a Decade in 3D Printing with Multiple New Product Launches « Fabbaloo
excerpts:
Unsurprisingly, Creality took the anniversary opportunity to launch several new products. They announce new products every few months, so an anniversary product announcement is perfectly natural.

The new products covered quite a range of functionality. Let’s take a look at what was announced.

The new K2 Plus 3D printer [Source: Creality]

The big announcement was the new K2 Plus 3D printer, which not only significantly improves performance and quality, but now includes an optional four-spool filament switching attachment, the “Creality Filament System”. We wrote about the [K2 Plus](https://www.fabbaloo.com/news/creality-launches-k2-plus-with-multicolor-capabilities) earlier this week.

The Ender-3 V3 3D printer [Source: Creality]

Creality surprisingly improved their [just-released Ender-3 V3](https://www.fabbaloo.com/news/creality-launches-ender-3-v3-with-innovative-corexz-system-for-enhanced-speed-and-quality) with unique CoreXZ technology with the Ender-3 V3 Plus.
The Plus version inherits all of the original Ender-3 V3’s features, such as the quick-swap hardened nozzle, 4.3” touch screen, high speed printing, advanced cooling design, etc., but combines them with a much larger build volume: 300 x 300 x 350 mm.

The HALOT-Mage S 14K resin 3D printer [Source: Creality]

A new resin 3D printer was included in the announcement: the HALOT-Mage S 14K provides for high quality prints with its massive 14K mono LCD light engine. This machine can print objects at the rapid rate of 150mm per hour, and includes onboard air filtration.

Did you know that Creality manufacturers products other than 3D printers? They’ve offered a line of laser cutters for a couple of years now, and they just announced a new model, the Creality Falcon2 Pro 60W. This fully enclosed laser cutter is quite powerful. If you’re not familiar, a 60W power laser is easily able to cut through thick wood, making it extremely capable.
Two 3D scanners were also announced, the CR-Scan Otter and the CR-Scan Raptor. The Raptor is designed for industrial use for metrology applications, while the Otter is a more general use device. Both seem to have a number of advanced features one would not have seen in low cost 3D scanners years ago.

Creality expanded their 3D print materials offering, and now boasts of 50 different colors for their filament lines. This year they also introduced an RFID identification for spools, which should be very useful with the new Creality Filament System.

As always, Creality offers these products along with their existing product lines at both their online store and at Amazon.

# Orbbec and Creality Launch Pika, Bringing 3D Scanning into the Pocket Era

02 Jun 2026 | By [Natalia de la Rosa](https://www.autonomyglobal.co/author/natdlrs/)

**2 June 2026:** [Creality](https://www.creality.com/) unveiled Pika, a next-generation AI-powered portable 3D scanner co-developed with [Orbbec](https://www.orbbec.com/) , during its 12th Anniversary “AI Ecosystem” product launch event.

Powered by Orbbec’s core underlying technologies, Pika breaks the mold of traditional 3D scanners by combining high-precision scanning, intelligent AI computing, and an ultra-portable design into one compact device. This launch marks a significant leap forward in integrated hardware and software innovation for the 3D scanning industry.

**Orbbec and Creality Deepen Strategic Partnership**
Creality, the global consumer 3D printing ecosystem leader, officially debuted on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. On the same day, Orbbec and Creality announced a deepened strategic partnership, including the establishment of a “3D Scanner Digital Joint Innovation Center” and the joint development of a next-generation “3D Printing AI Vision Intelligent Platform”.

Built upon technological innovation and ecosystem collaboration, the partnership aims to accelerate the high-quality development of the 3D printing industry, empowering creators and digital manufacturing enterprises worldwide.

Against this backdrop of strategic collaboration and AI-driven innovation, the two companies officially unveiled Pika during Creality’s 12th Anniversary “AI Ecosystem” product launch event — a next-generation AI-powered portable 3D scanner co-developed by Orbbec and Creality. **Ultra-Portable Design for 3D Scanning**
